newsitem.title: USA: Judge says "criminal culture" at Merrill, Lazard.
newsitem.headline: Judge says "criminal culture" at Merrill, Lazard.

text.p: A federal judge overseeing sentencing in a major municipal bond fraud case on Wednesday blasted Merrill Lynch & Co and Lazard Freres & Co for what he called a "corporate criminal culture."

U.S. District Judge William Young criticized the firms during a sentencing hearing for former Lazard muni adviser Mark Ferber, who was convicted in August of fraud and conspiracy in connection with his ties to Merrill Lynch & Co..
"By a fair preponderance of the evidence, I see nothing that shows that this (relationship between the two firms) is contrary to the corporate culture of Merrill Lynch and Lazard Freres," Young said.
The allegations centered on whether or not a contract between Ferber and Merrill was adequately disclosed to Ferber's government clients in the municipal bond market.
Both firms settled the matter with the U.S. Attorneys Office last year by paying a total of $24 million in fines. Neither firm admitted or denied guilt in connection with the settlement.
